questions.label: Q1
questions.question: Does the claim state that, together with the rent increase, the landlord gave notice of termination?

questions.label: Q2
questions.question: Does the increase notice give, as its reason, higher costs for the landlord (for example higher mortgage interest or operating costs) or additional services or works by the landlord (for example a renovation)?

questions.label: Q3
questions.question: Does the claim state that the increase applies a clause of the lease linking the rent to an index (such as the Swiss consumer price index)?

questions.label: Q4
questions.question: Does the claim state that the increase is a step fixed in advance in the lease, by which the rent rises periodically by fixed amounts (graduated rent)?

questions.label: Q5
questions.question: Does the claim state that the landlord has announced, demanded or charged a higher rent for the dwelling, by a notice, a letter, an invoice or otherwise (whether or not on an official form)?

text:
Hi,

This may be a strange one, so bear with me. I live at Hauptstrasse 104 in Wohlen and rent my flat from Moosacker Trading Ltd. On 6 March 2026 my neighbour across the landing, Leo Morgan, showed me a letter he had just received from Moosacker telling him his rent was going up. He was furious, and naturally I assumed my letter was on its way too.

It never came. I have checked my post every day for a month. Moosacker has not sent me any letter or form about my rent, Mr Leo Graf at the office has not said a word about it on the phone or in person, and my payment slips for April and May still show the same CHF 3190 as always. As far as I can see, nobody has asked me for a single franc more.

My worry is this: I've heard there are short deadlines with this kind of thing. What if a letter was sent and got lost in the post, or went to my old address? Could I then be stuck with a higher rent without ever having had the chance to respond? Or is it simply the case that, as long as I've received nothing, nothing has changed for me?

I'd appreciate a short answer so I can stop lying awake over it.

Thanks,
Felix Huber
